solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detective left loads in front of sergeant

indicators.note: to load something is to put it inside, so one piece goes into another
the front of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: to be home is to be in, not out
L is the standard abbreviation for left
the opening letter of sergeant

explanation.surface: A police detective dumps a pile of work on the sergeant standing beside him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is not a link word here: it stands for HOME, as in 'stay home' or 'stay in'. L goes inside it, then the S of sergeant follows to make HOLMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherlock Holmes is the most famous fictional private investigator, so his surname is a natural example of a sleuth.

clue.text: Moor closed in northerly direction – what’s this?

indicators.note: in a down entry, heading north means reading from the bottom up, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: a door pulled to is closed
'hello, what's this?' is the exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone finds a stretch of moorland shut off to the north and wonders what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moor' looks like open heathland, but it is the capital-M Moor of Venice. TO for closed comes from the phrase 'push the door to'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragic hero is described in the play's full title as the Moor of Venice, a North African general.

clue.text: Guy receives very good partner in department store

indicators.note: whoever receives something takes it in, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: a guy is a man
an adverb of approval, as in 'just so'

explanation.surface: A man in a department store is given a top-notch business partner.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN takes in SO. The theme of the puzzle is famous pairs, and each 'partner in' clue wants the other half of a well-known double act.
explanation.definitionFit: Fortnum & Mason is the grand London department store on Piccadilly, founded by a footman and his landlord in 1707.

clue.text: In contest it challenged interplanetary partner

indicators.note: the word sits inside the run of letters that follows, spanning several words

blocks.note: the run of letters across these three words contains the answer

explanation.surface: Within some competition, a particular entrant was challenged.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs from the end of 'contest' through 'it' into 'challenged'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Disney film Lilo & Stitch, Stitch is an alien experiment who crash-lands on Hawaii and becomes the girl's companion.

clue.text: It hurts that girlfriend’s swiped oriental slipper

indicators.note: to swipe is to snatch and hold on to, so one piece ends up held inside another

blocks.note: babe is a slang term for a girlfriend
the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone complains that his girlfriend has nicked a Turkish slipper, or struck him with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slipper' looks like a thief here alongside 'swiped', but it is footwear; 'girlfriend's' is short for 'girlfriend has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A babouche is a heelless leather slipper worn in Morocco and the Middle East, the East in old usage.

clue.text: Partner in ices, in the north, raised bill

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising letters puts the bottom at the top, so they read backwards

blocks.note: neb is a northern English and Scots word for a beak, a regional usage flagged by the words before it

explanation.surface: An ice-cream business partner up north puts the prices up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the north' flags a regional word: neb, the beak of a bird. 'Raised bill' sounds like a price rise but is a beak turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben & Jerry's ice cream was founded by Ben Cohen and Jerry Greenfield in Vermont, so Ben is one half of the pair.

clue.text: Old bank partner runs probes damaging to daughter

indicators.note: a probe pushes inside something, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: bad for you means damaging
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
'bad to' and 'bad for' mean the same here
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A former partner at a bank runs investigations that hurt his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damaging to daughter' is a phrase spelt out almost literally, with 'to' swapped for its synonym 'for'; runs is the cricket R.
explanation.definitionFit: Bradford & Bingley was a British building society turned bank, nationalised in 2008, so it is now an old name.

clue.text: Condition is painful for priest: ordeal exposed

indicators.note: to expose is to strip off the covering, so each word loses its outermost letters

blocks.note: is painful means hurts; drop the outside letters
a priest is a vicar; drop the outside letters
an ordeal is a trial; drop the outside letters

explanation.surface: A vicar finds his condition painful, his suffering now out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exposed' applies to all three words: HURTS, VICAR and TRIAL each lose their first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Urticaria is the medical name for hives, an itchy skin rash named after the stinging nettle.

clue.text: Completely naked with partner in health food shop

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outer letters go and the inside is kept

blocks.note: completely means wholly; strip the outer letters
and means with, joining two things

explanation.surface: Someone strips off entirely, along with a business partner, in a health food store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Completely naked' reads as one phrase, but 'naked' works on WHOLLY alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Holland & Barrett is the UK high-street chain selling vitamins and health foods, so Holland is one partner in its name.

clue.text: Son blocking love from romantic film actor

indicators.note: taking something from a word means removing it
to block is to stand in the way, sitting in the middle of another word

blocks.note: The Piano is Jane Campion's 1993 romantic drama
love is zero in tennis, so O
S is the standard abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A son gets in the way of the love scenes in a romantic film's leading man.
explanation.walkthrough: THE PIANO loses its final O (love), and S goes in after THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thespis was the first actor of Greek tragedy, so a thespian is a performer on stage.

clue.text: After series of races, I will cut a murderous figure

indicators.note: the setter takes the opening letter of this word as its own contribution, an unusual liberty
cutting something short trims off its end

blocks.note: the opening letter
the TT is the Isle of Man motorbike Tourist Trophy series
I will shortens to I'LL, which loses its last letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Once a run of races is over, someone vows to cut a dash as a killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening A is a liberty: blog commenters called it the kind of trick only this setter gets away with. The rest is TT, I'LL cut short, and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila the Hun led brutal invasions of the Roman Empire in the fifth century and became a byword for savagery.

clue.text: Fan emerging from oddly functional design

indicators.note: something emerging from a place leaves it, so those letters come out
oddly means in a strange way, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A fan comes out of a quirkily practical piece of design.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts a solver to take alternate letters; here it shuffles what is left of FUNCTIONAL once F, A and N are removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A linocut is a print made from a carved block of linoleum, so it is a design or artwork.

clue.text: Food checker ingesting trace of opioid brown bread because of it?

indicators.note: a trace is the faintest mark, so only one opening letter is taken
ingesting is swallowing, taking something inside

blocks.note: a taster samples food for safety
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A royal food taster swallows a hint of an opioid and ends up dead because of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown bread' is rhyming slang for dead, which the surface leans on; read straight it means bread browned by the appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the kitchen appliance is the thing that turns slices of bread brown.

clue.text: Spa offering something tripper drops briefly in river

indicators.note: saying a word briefly cuts it short, so its last letter goes
one piece placed in another sits inside it

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
LSD, acid, is dropped by someone tripping

explanation.surface: A spa treatment is something a day tripper drops into for a short while at a riverside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tripper' looks like a holidaymaker but is someone on a hallucinogenic trip; to drop acid is to take LSD.
explanation.definitionFit: A facial is a beauty treatment for the skin of the face, a staple service at health spas.

clue.text: The establishment backs poor old partner in fashion house

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order
to back is to come up behind, so one piece follows the other

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: The Establishment supports an impoverished former partner of a fashion label.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The establishment' is the Church of England, the established church, abbreviated CE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolce & Gabbana is the Italian fashion house founded by Domenico Dolce and Stefano Gabbana.

clue.text: Work a miracle bandaging head in hygienic fabric

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it into a new form
the head of a word is its opening letter
a bandage wraps round something, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A medic works a miracle, wrapping an injured head in clean cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head in hygienic' looks like a bandaged head; it is just the first letter of hygienic, which sits in the middle of the shuffled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Camel hair is a soft textile woven from the underwool of camels, used for classic overcoats.

clue.text: Market rated for reviving direct deals

indicators.note: reviving something brings it back in a new form, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: a fair is a market
taken as written

explanation.surface: A market's credit rating is judged by whether it can revive straight dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For reviving' reads oddly: 'for' is the link and 'reviving' works on RATED.
explanation.definitionFit: The movement buys directly from producers at guaranteed prices, cutting out middlemen to give growers a fairer return.

clue.text: Partner in game dropping periods?

blocks.note: animal droppings are dung
an eon is a vast period of time

explanation.surface: A doubles partner in a match keeps missing whole sessions of play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dropping periods' reads as a verb phrase, but it splits into the noun 'dropping' and 'periods'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungeons & Dragons is the fantasy role-playing game launched in 1974, so this is half of its title.

clue.text: Here we are in Cornwall, and I’m 50 per cent sure this is beachwear

indicators.note: fifty per cent is half, so only the first half of the word is kept

blocks.note: Cornwall is in the south-west, SW
taken as written
the first half
it's is a contraction of 'it is', standing for 'this is'

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker in Cornwall is only half sure that what they are wearing counts as beachwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Here we are in Cornwall' is a roundabout way of naming the region the county sits in, the South West.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimming costumes are the standard clothing for bathing at the seaside, the obvious items worn on sand.

clue.text: Honnold, maybe, partner in franchise

blocks.note: Alex Honnold climbed the rock wall of El Capitan without ropes
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: The rock climber Alex Honnold, perhaps, as a partner in some business franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Honnold, the American free soloist of El Capitan, is a wall ace: an expert at climbing sheer rock faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallace & Gromit is the Aardman animation series about a cheese-loving inventor and his dog.

clue.text: After sunny holiday you’ll see this cop’s partner in film

definitions.text: After sunny holiday you’ll see this

blocks.clueFragment: After sunny holiday you’ll see this
blocks.note: split three and two, the answer says what happens to your colour a few weeks after a sunny break
the 1989 buddy-cop film pairs two detectives

explanation.surface: Back from a sunny break, you'll spot this detective's sidekick in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as TAN GO, the first part describes a holiday tan fading away. The second points to Tango & Cash, starring Sylvester Stallone and Kurt Russell.
explanation.definitionFit: Ray Tango, played by Sylvester Stallone, is one of the two police officers in the action film Tango & Cash.

clue.text: In the ascent, say, tailed trapped carnivore

indicators.note: climbing up a down entry means reading from bottom to top, so the letters run backwards
to tail something is to cut off its tail, the final letter

blocks.note: e.g. means for example, as does 'say'
caught in a net

explanation.surface: On a climb, an animal is followed and then caught in a trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailed' looks like 'followed', but here it means docked of its tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A genette, or genet, is a spotted cat-like mammal of Africa and southern Europe that hunts small prey.

clue.text: Barrel quaffed by plucky partner in consumer goods

indicators.note: something quaffed is swallowed, so it ends up inside the drinker

blocks.note: game means brave and willing
bl is the abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: A spirited business partner downs a whole barrel of something.
explanation.walkthrough: GAME swallows BL, the abbreviation used for barrels of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Procter & Gamble is the American multinational making household products such as detergents and toiletries.

clue.text: First of lifelong delinquents thrown back into gaol, sadly

definitions.note: plural in the clue, while the answer names one such habitual offender

indicators.note: the first of each word is its opening letter
throwing something back sends it the other way, so the letters run backwards
something done sadly is done badly, so these letters come out in a muddled order
one piece placed into another goes inside it

blocks.note: the opening letters of both words
taken as written

explanation.surface: Habitual young offenders are sent back to prison, which is a sad state of affairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters are taken from two words, reversed, and set inside the rearranged GAOL. Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Old lag is British slang for a habitual criminal who has spent years in and out of prison.

clue.text: Publicity material bagged by Italian itinerant

indicators.note: something bagged is put into a bag, so it ends up inside

blocks.note: a Roman is an Italian from Rome
an ad is an advertisement

explanation.surface: An Italian wanderer stuffs advertising leaflets into his bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian itinerant' reads as one person, but 'Italian' is wordplay and 'itinerant' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadman is one who spends his life on the road, a wanderer, though in modern UK slang it means a street youth.

clue.text: High street partner has fun multiplying capital by 20

indicators.note: multiplying a Roman numeral by twenty turns it into a different numeral, swapping one letter for another

blocks.note: to lark about is to have fun; its capital L is the Roman numeral 50, and 50 times 20 is 1000, M

explanation.surface: A high-street business partner enjoys himself by making twenty times the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but is the first letter. L is 50 in Roman numerals; times 20 gives 1000, M.
explanation.definitionFit: Marks & Spencer is the long-established British department store chain found on almost every main shopping street.

clue.text: This involves washing facilities, given a reason to wash?

blocks.note: the facilities is a euphemism for the toilet, a lav
taken as written
BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A note on how a building's washing facilities give people a reason to clean up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Washing facilities' reads as one phrase, but the clue splits after 'washing': 'facilities' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The lavabo is the priest's ritual hand-washing at Mass, and also the basin used for it.

clue.text: Appropriate line followed by one rocket

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for line
I is the Roman numeral one
a rocket is a severe telling-off

explanation.surface: A suitable route is followed by a single rocket launch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' wants to be an adjective, but it is the verb meaning to take. A rocket is British slang for a dressing-down, here used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberate is jocular slang for stealing, so to liberate goods is to appropriate them without permission.

clue.text: Saucy partner dropping cap of beer

indicators.note: in a down entry the cap is the top letter, and dropping it moves it to the bottom

blocks.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A cheeky companion knocks the top off a bottle of beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saucy' sounds cheeky, but it is literal: the answer is half of a sauce brand. The top letter of ALE drops to the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Lea & Perrins is the maker of Worcestershire sauce, named after chemists John Lea and William Perrins.

clue.text: Distraught banker admits what state Lincoln’s in

indicators.note: someone distraught is all over the place, so the letters are jumbled
to admit is to let in, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
as is a dialect relative pronoun meaning what or who

explanation.surface: A frantic banker confesses the mess Abraham Lincoln is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lincoln' looks like the president but is a city: Lincoln is the capital of Nebraska.
explanation.definitionFit: Lincoln is the capital city of the American Midwestern state of Nebraska, so that is where it sits.

clue.text: The conclusion of Harrogate flower festival

indicators.note: the conclusion of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter
the aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: The closing day of the Harrogate flower festival.
explanation.walkthrough: Harrogate is a Yorkshire spa town famous for its flower shows, which makes 'flower festival' read as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter is the Christian feast celebrating the resurrection, one of the main holidays of the church year.
